prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
competitors_mentioned: Use the Missouri Department of Commerce
answer_verbatim:
For a self-employed person in Kansas City, the “best” choice is usually an **independent, Missouri-licensed health-insurance broker who is registered to sell Marketplace/ACA plans through HealthCare.gov**—not a broker tied to only one insurer.

I would start with:

1. **HealthCare.gov “Find Local Help”**  
   Search your Kansas City ZIP code and select an **agent/broker**. This is the most reliable way to find brokers who can enroll you in both subsidized Marketplace plans and off-Marketplace plans.  
   https://www.healthcare.gov/find-local-help/

2. **Cover Missouri / Enroll Missouri** for unbiased enrollment help  
   If you want assistance that is not sales-driven, Missouri’s navigator organizations can help compare Marketplace options and subsidies. They are especially useful if your self-employment income varies.  
   https://covermissouri.org/

3. **Verify the broker’s Missouri license** before enrolling  
   Use the Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance license lookup. Make sure the person is active and licensed for health insurance.  
   https://insurance.mo.gov/

When speaking with a broker, ask these questions:

- “Are you independent, and which carriers do you represent in Jackson/Clay/Platte County?”
- “Can you enroll me through **HealthCare.gov** if I qualify for premium tax credits?”
- “Will you compare on- and off-Marketplace plans?”
- “Do you work with self-employed clients whose income changes during the year?”
- “Do you charge me a fee beyond carrier commission?”
- “Will you help me update my income estimate if my business income changes?”

For most self-employed people, a Marketplace plan is the first place to look because subsidies can substantially reduce premiums. Your eligibility is based on your projected annual household income—not just your business revenue—and you may also qualify for the self-employed health-insurance tax deduction.

Avoid any broker who immediately pushes short-term medical, fixed-indemnity, health-sharing, or “private PPO” plans without first showing you ACA-compliant Marketplace options. Those products can have major coverage gaps.

If you want, tell me your age, household size, estimated 2026 income, and Kansas City ZIP code, and I can outline the types of plans and subsidy range you should ask a broker to compare.
